observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a hydraulic press with yellow-and-black diagonally striped cylinders. A lower striped platform holds a bullet casing that is already flattened on its left (brass base) end and tapers to a copper tip on the right, lying horizontally. A plain light-gray wall with a small brown smudge forms the background. The upper striped ram hangs above the casing with a visible gap.
visible_changes: The entire upper ram assembly (metal cap, yellow cone, and striped cylinder) translates downward steadily across the segment, reducing the vertical gap between the ram's bottom edge and the casing.
The lower platform and the casing remain essentially fixed in position and orientation; the casing's overall shape (flattened left, pointed right) does not change noticeably within this excerpt.
No camera movement is evident: the background smudge and platform keep constant positions relative to the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happened before the segment (the casing already appears pre-crushed; the onset of any deformation is not shown).
Whether the ram ultimately makes contact and further compresses the casing after the last frame.
The cause/operator driving the press descent.
uncertain_details: Whether the casing experiences any subtle additional compression as the ram nears it; the change is too small to confirm within these frames.
The exact moment of ram-casing contact, which is not reached inside the excerpt.
